question_en: What is the difference between a homestay and a Bed & Breakfast under government rules?
answer: Under the Ministry of Tourism scheme text, a homestay is a home where the owner lives on the property with the family. A B&B is a property where the owner does not live there and a manager looks after it. Both are limited to 1 to 6 lettable rooms (12 beds). Your state may use its own definition.
actions: Decide if you or a family member will live in the house while guests stay.
Count how many rooms you can let out to guests.
Ask your District Tourism Office which definition your state uses.
caution: The wording comes from an older uploaded copy of the national scheme. Several states have their own definitions and room limits.
context_needed: do you live in the house
evidence: Scheme eligibility text: homestay = owner resides with family, 1-6 rooms, 12 beds; B&B = owner not resident, agent manages (S53). 2022 strategy also says maximum 6 lettable rooms (S54).
verify_with: District Tourism Officer / State Tourism Department

question_en: Is it compulsory to get my homestay classified by the Ministry of Tourism?
answer: No. The Ministry of Tourism says its Incredible India homestay classification is a voluntary scheme. But many states have their own registration and some now require it. So you may still need a state registration even if the central scheme is voluntary.
actions: Check your state's homestay rules first, before applying centrally.
Ask the District Tourism Office if registration is compulsory in your state.
Consider the voluntary central classification later, once you are running well.
caution: Operating without a registration that your state requires can lead to penalties (for example, Himachal Pradesh reports a Rs 1 lakh fine). Rules are state-wise.
evidence: Ministry statements (21 Jul 2025 and NIDHI release): voluntary scheme with Gold and Silver categories. State enforcement example from a news report (S65).
verify_with: State Tourism Department / District Tourism Officer

question_en: What does Gold or Silver category mean for a homestay?
answer: Gold and Silver are the two classes of the Ministry of Tourism homestay classification. They show how complete the facilities are. Inspectors check mandatory and desirable items such as clean rooms, attached bathroom, safe water, clean kitchen, breakfast, fire safety equipment and a guest register. Gold asks for more than Silver.
actions: Read the checklist for Gold and Silver before you spend money on upgrades.
Fix the mandatory items first, then add desirable items over time.
Apply for the category you can meet today.
caution: State schemes use their own names (for example Kerala has Diamond, Gold and Silver; Gujarat has Silver, Gold and Platinum). Do not mix them.
evidence: National scheme: two categories Gold and Silver (S51, S52); mandatory/desirable checklist in older scheme text (S53). Kerala and Gujarat naming from their own pages (S63, S68).
verify_with: NIDHI+ portal / State Tourism Department

question_en: How do I apply for the Ministry of Tourism homestay classification?
answer: The older scheme text says to apply online, pay the fee digitally, and wait for an inspection by a regional committee. It listed Rs 3,000 for Silver and Rs 5,000 for Gold, a 2-year validity, and documents like ownership papers, police clearance and photographs. The Ministry now runs the NIDHI+ portal, so confirm the current steps and fees there.
actions: Open the NIDHI+ website and read the homestay classification guidelines.
Collect ownership papers, ID, photos of rooms and kitchen, and police clearance.
Ask the Regional Office of the Ministry of Tourism if you are stuck.
caution: Fees, portal and forms may have changed since the older scheme text. Do not pay anyone who promises a quick approval. Apply only on the official portal.
evidence: Scheme text: online application, Rs 3,000 Silver / Rs 5,000 Gold, 2-year validity, documents, inspection (S53). NIDHI as current data portal (S52).
verify_with: NIDHI+ portal / Ministry of Tourism regional office

question_en: What do I actually get if my homestay is classified or registered with the Ministry?
answer: The Ministry says there is no direct money under its classification scheme. Benefits are indirect: a national listing, a quality tag guests can trust, and a base to apply for other schemes. Some states give subsidies on top of this. Ask your state.
actions: Do not expect cash from the central classification itself.
Ask your state tourism department what subsidy or loan help it gives to registered homestays.
Use your registration number in your listings so guests can trust you.
caution: Beware of agents who promise a central subsidy for classification. The Ministry has stated there is none under this scheme.
evidence: Ministry statements: no financial assistance under the classification scheme (Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha replies and NIDHI release, 2025).
verify_with: State Tourism Department

question_en: What is the NIDHI portal and do I have to register on it?
answer: NIDHI is the Ministry of Tourism's national database of hotels, homestays and other tourism units. The Ministry says it is for collecting data on registered and classified units. It is not a booking site. It checks identity (PAN, OTP) and, where needed, a food licence.
actions: Ask your District Tourism Office whether your state asks you to register on NIDHI as well.
Keep your PAN, mobile number and, if you serve food, your food licence ready.
Do not treat NIDHI as a place that brings guests by itself.
caution: Some states earlier used NIDHI as their only route; others now have their own portals. Follow your state's current process.
evidence: PIB release on NIDHI: data gathering, not a booking platform, no occupancy tracking (S52). UP news report says homestays earlier registered only on NIDHI before its state policy (S76).
verify_with: District Tourism Officer

question_en: Has the government made new homestay rules that replace the old Bed & Breakfast scheme?
answer: The Ministry now refers to 'Incredible India Homestay Establishments' classification and the NIDHI portal. In December 2025 it described a NITI Aayog report with suggestions to states: a simple registration capped at 30 days, one-window digital approval, and homes charged at residential rates for water, power and property tax. These are suggestions, not a law. States still decide.
actions: Check your state's latest homestay policy page or ask the District Tourism Office.
Ask whether your state has adopted the 30-day, single-window idea.
Keep copies of all papers, since formats change often.
caution: I could not open the current national guideline document itself. Treat the central scheme details as needing a check on NIDHI+.
evidence: Ministry release of 15 Dec 2025 describing NITI Aayog roadmap (S50); 2025 statements naming Incredible India Homestay Establishments scheme (S51, S52).
verify_with: Ministry of Tourism / NIDHI+ portal

question_en: Is there any government money or loan to build or upgrade rooms for homestay?
answer: Central support known from Ministry statements: collateral-free Mudra loans for homestays announced in Budget 2025-26, and for tribal villages under PM Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan, up to Rs 5 lakh for two new rooms per household, Rs 3 lakh for renovation, and community facilities. Many states add their own subsidy. Amounts and eligibility are decided by each scheme.
actions: Ask your tourism office whether your village is in a PM-JUGA tribal area.
Visit a bank or Mudra lender with your room plan and costs.
Check your state scheme (several states have one) before you start building.
caution: Do not start construction before approval if a scheme says it must be pre-approved. Never pay an agent for a grant.
evidence: Ministry statements on Mudra loans (Budget 2025-26) and PM-JUGA homestay support: Rs 5 lakh new rooms, Rs 3 lakh renovation (S51, S55), Feb 2026.
verify_with: District Tourism Officer / Tribal Affairs office / bank

question_en: What is the National Strategy for Promotion of Rural Homestays? Does it apply to me?
answer: It is a 2022 Ministry of Tourism paper that advises states how to support rural homestays. It suggests a limit of 6 lettable rooms, relief from heavy licence burdens, power and water at domestic rates, a possible subsidy and registration on NIDHI. It is advice to states, so it does not give you rights by itself.
actions: Ask your state tourism department which of these suggestions your state has adopted.
Quote the strategy politely when asking for domestic electricity or water rates.
Look for your state's own homestay order for what is binding.
caution: Do not tell guests or neighbours that you are entitled to these benefits just because they are in the strategy.
evidence: National Strategy for Promotion of Rural Homestays 2022 (Ministry PDF); recommendations to states.
verify_with: State Tourism Department

question_en: How many rooms can I have and still call it a homestay?
answer: It depends on your state. The national scheme and many state policies say 1 to 6 lettable rooms. Goa says 2 to 6. Haryana says up to 5. Reports say Uttarakhand (2026 revision) and Bihar's scheme allow 8. If you have more rooms, you may fall under a guest house or lodge category with different rules.
actions: Count only the rooms you let out to guests.
Check your state's rule for the room limit before you build.
Ask the Tourism Office what category you fall in if you plan more rooms.
caution: Uttarakhand and Bihar figures are from news reports. Confirm on the state order.
evidence: National 1-6 rooms (S53); Goa 2-6 (S66); Haryana up to 5 (S70); Gujarat 1-6 (S68); Uttarakhand 8 rooms/24 beds and Bihar 8 rooms from news reports (S75, S73).
verify_with: District Tourism Officer

question_en: Should I start a homestay, a farmstay, a B&B or a camping site?
answer: Homestay means guests stay in or beside your family home. B&B means the owner does not live there and it is managed by someone. Farmstay or agri-tourism means guests live on a working farm. Camping means tents in an open space. Each can fall under different rules. Start with what you already have: spare rooms, a farm, or a safe open field.
actions: Write down what you have: rooms, farm activities, land and water.
Ask your tourism office which category your plan falls under.
Start small with one or two rooms or one tent and learn from guests.
caution: Camping and farm activities may need permissions from land, forest or panchayat authorities. Maharashtra has a separate agri-tourism policy that allows temporary tents and tree houses; other states differ.
evidence: Homestay vs B&B definitions (S53); Maharashtra Tourism Policy 2024 covers agri-tourism, tents, tree houses (S74). Choice guidance is general practice.
verify_with: State Tourism Department / Agriculture Department

question_en: Whom do I ask for help to register my homestay: tourism office, panchayat or block office?
answer: Start with the District Tourism Officer (or the Tourism Department office for your district). Some states list this officer as the one who inspects your home or sits on the approval committee. Also meet your Gram Panchayat, since local approvals and records often pass through it. The Block Development Office can guide you on rural schemes.
actions: Call or visit the district Tourism Office and ask for the homestay registration process.
Take your ID and ownership papers with you.
Tell the Gram Panchayat that you plan to host guests.
caution: Names of offices differ by state. Do not pay anyone who is not a government officer for 'approval'.
evidence: Andhra Pradesh: District Tourism Officer inspects (S77); Kerala: District Deputy Director is notified of changes (S63); Ladakh: applications go to Assistant Director Tourism of district (S69).
verify_with: District Tourism Officer

question_en: Do I need an NOC from my Gram Panchayat to run a homestay?
answer: It depends on your state. Himachal Pradesh reports say units must register with the tourism department and the local body or panchayat. Uttar Pradesh requires NOCs from local bodies in its 2025 policy (news report). Goa asks for trade licence and local authority NOCs. Other states may differ.
actions: Ask your tourism office whether a panchayat NOC is part of your state's process.
Visit the Gram Panchayat office and ask for the procedure and any fee.
Keep a copy of the NOC with your registration papers.
caution: These points come from state pages and news reports. Confirm with the tourism office for your state.
evidence: HP: register with tourism dept and panchayat (S65, news); Goa: trade licence and local authority NOCs listed among documents (S66); UP: NOCs from local bodies (S76, news).
verify_with: District Tourism Officer / Gram Panchayat

question_en: How do I register my homestay in Kerala?
answer: In Kerala, the Department of Tourism classifies homestays as Diamond, Gold or Silver. You apply online and pay a non-refundable fee (Rs 3,750 as shown on the page). Only owner-occupied homes qualify; leased or rented houses do not. Up to 6 rooms are allowed. A committee inspects, and the Director of Tourism issues the order. It is valid for 3 years.
actions: Open the Kerala Tourism homestay classification section and read the guidelines and document list.
Apply online and pay the fee, then get ready for the inspection committee visit.
Apply for reclassification 3 months before the 3 years end.
caution: You must display the certificate to guests, tell the District Deputy Director about changes within 30 days, and be ready for surprise inspections. Fee may change, so check the portal.
evidence: Kerala classification guidelines page: owner-occupied, max 6 rooms, Rs 3,750 fee, 3-year validity, display and 30-day change notice (S63). Quorum-based inspection noted in Ministry release (S50).
verify_with: District Tourism Office, Kerala / Department of Tourism (0471-2321132)

question_en: How do I register my homestay in Himachal Pradesh?
answer: Himachal Pradesh notified Home Stay Rules in June 2025 (as per a secondary summary). Registration is online through HP Tourism eServices. Categories are Silver, Gold and Diamond. The summary says up to 6 rooms, and fees depend on area type and category (rural panchayat areas cost less). Women owners and the remote Pangi area get discounts. Existing homestays were asked to re-register.
actions: Open HP Tourism eServices and start the homestay registration.
Prepare ownership papers, photos, and fire and safety items listed in the rules.
Ask the District Tourism Office about the fee for your area type.
caution: The rules are described from a secondary summary and the 2025 draft numbers differ from the final. Do not rely on any fee quoted here; check on the eServices portal. Gold and Diamond homes may face commercial utility rates.
evidence: TeamLease RegTech summary of HP Home Stay Rules, 2025 notified 25 Jun 2025: online registration, Silver/Gold/Diamond, max 6 rooms, fees by area, discounts for women and Pangi.
verify_with: District Tourism Development Officer, HP / HP Tourism eServices

question_en: What happens in Himachal if I run a homestay without registering?
answer: A news report says Himachal Pradesh plans a fine of Rs 1 lakh for illegal homestays and, on repeat violations, disconnection of water and electricity. Units must register with the tourism department and also with their local body or panchayat.
actions: Register with the tourism department as early as possible.
Also inform your local body or panchayat as the rules require.
Keep your registration certificate where inspectors can see it.
caution: This is from a news report, not the official notification. Check current penalties with the Tourism Department.
evidence: The Tribune report on HP crackdown following 25 Jun 2025 rules: Rs 1 lakh fine, disconnection on repeat violations, registration with tourism dept and local bodies.
verify_with: District Tourism Development Officer, HP

question_en: How do I register my homestay in Uttarakhand?
answer: Uttarakhand's Tourism Development Board registers homestays online. A May 2026 news report says the scheme was revised to allow up to 8 rooms and 24 beds, validity of 5 years, and group-level Community Based Tourism Units of 8 to 10 homestays. The older rule said purely residential premises with 1 to 6 rooms. Check which version applies to you.
actions: Visit the Uttarakhand Tourism homestay registration portal for the current form and fees.
Ask your District Tourism Office whether your village or nagar panchayat is covered.
Keep ownership papers and ID ready.
caution: The 2026 details come from a news report and the older rule text could not be verified here. Confirm with the Uttarakhand Tourism Development Board.
evidence: ETV Bharat report dated 20 May 2026 on revised scheme: 8 rooms, 24 beds, 5-year validity, online process, community tourism units.
verify_with: Uttarakhand Tourism Development Board / District Tourism Officer

question_en: Can I lease my homestay to someone else to run in Sikkim?
answer: A September 2023 report says the Sikkim Tourism Department no longer allows homestay owners to lease or rent their homestay to third parties. Owners must run it themselves. This is under the Sikkim Registration of Homestay Establishment Rules, 2013.
actions: Run the homestay yourself or with family members.
Ask the Sikkim Tourism Department before any arrangement with a manager.
Keep your registration certificate in your own name.
caution: Based on a news report; ask the department for the written advisory.
evidence: Curly Tales report of Sept 2023 advisory under Sikkim Registration of Homestay Establishment Rules 2013.
verify_with: Sikkim Tourism and Civil Aviation Department

question_en: Is there any support to build a homestay in Meghalaya?
answer: Meghalaya has the Chief Minister's Meghalaya Homestay Mission Scheme. A scheme listing says new homestays need proof of land ownership or a registered lease of at least 7 years and must use one of the department-approved designs. Support is up to 70 percent of project cost, with extra for upgrades. Applications are online with checks by district and state committees.
actions: Visit the Meghalaya Tourism portal and read the scheme page.
Keep land papers or your registered lease ready.
Pick a standard design before you start any building.
caution: Details come from a scheme listing, not the department portal. Percentages and limits may change.
evidence: publicservicesmap.in listing of Chief Minister's Meghalaya Homestay Mission Scheme: eligibility, up to 70% support, online application.
verify_with: Meghalaya Tourism Department / District Tourism Officer

question_en: How do I register my homestay in Goa?
answer: The Goa Tourism page describes a homestay as an owner-occupied home with 2 to 6 rooms and up to 12 beds. You apply offline at Paryatan Bhavan, Panaji or online on goaonline.gov.in. Listed papers are ownership proof, trade licence and local NOCs, and KYC. The annual fee shown is Rs 1,000. Homestays in seven named talukas can get incentives. A Dec 2025 Ministry release says Goa now needs only three documents with 5-year validity.
actions: Check the Goa Tourism homestay policy page for the latest process.
Use the goaonline.gov.in portal if you want to apply online.
Keep ownership proof, ID and GST papers ready.
caution: The two sources describe different versions of Goa's process. Ask the Goa Tourism Department which one is in force.
evidence: Goa Tourism homestay policy page (S66): definitions, documents, Rs 1,000 fee, incentives; Ministry release Dec 2025 describes 3-document, 5-year process (S50).
verify_with: Department of Tourism, Goa (Paryatan Bhavan, Panaji)

question_en: How do I register my homestay in Karnataka?
answer: The Karnataka Department of Tourism has issued Revised Homestay Registration Guidelines 2025. The page says they cover registration, eligibility, documents, a domestic tax benefit and non-commercial status, and online permits under the Tourism Policy 2024-29. I could not open the PDF, so I cannot state rooms, fees or validity.
actions: Download the 2025 guidelines PDF from the Karnataka Tourism website.
Contact the Department of Tourism, Indhana Bhavan, Bengaluru (080-2235-2828) with questions.
Ask your District Tourism Office for the local inspection process.
caution: Fees, room limits and validity are not stated here because I could not verify them.
evidence: Karnataka Tourism web page announcing Revised Homestay Registration Guidelines 2025 (TOR-133-TDO-2025-G-O). Details of the PDF not read.
verify_with: Department of Tourism, Karnataka

question_en: How do I register my homestay in Gujarat?
answer: Under Gujarat's 2020 homestay policy, the home must be your principal residence where you live with family, with 1 to 6 rooms (12 beds). It is classified as Silver, Gold or Platinum. Steps are document check, police verification, field inspection and a committee review. The certificate is valid for 2 years. Homestays get residential electricity rates and residential municipal property and water tax.
actions: Read the Gujarat Homestay Policy 2020 on the Gujarat Tourism website.
Prepare the documents and apply for the category you meet.
Apply for police verification as part of the process.
caution: The fees printed in the 2020 policy (Silver Rs 500, Gold Rs 1,000, Platinum Rs 2,000) may have changed. Confirm with Gujarat Tourism.
evidence: Gujarat 'Policy for Registration of Homestay Establishments' PDF (2020): 1-6 rooms, categories and fees, verification steps, 2-year validity, residential rates.
verify_with: Tourism Corporation of Gujarat / Commissioner of Tourism

question_en: How do I register a homestay in Ladakh?
answer: Ladakh Homestay Policy 2023 supports homestays in rural areas outside Leh and Kargil municipal limits. You need 1 to 6 rooms, a winter-friendly flush toilet, be a Ladakh resident with registered, dispute-free land. Apply to the Assistant Director (Tourism) of your district. Field, district and UT committees review. New beneficiaries can get a support kit, winter toilet support (75 percent, up to Rs 1.25 lakh), and furnishing money.
actions: Meet the Assistant Director of Tourism in your district.
Prepare land papers and plan a winter-friendly toilet.
Be ready to run the homestay for at least 5 years.
caution: Owners must display a Proof of Listing, keep guest and billing records and serve meals. The policy is valid for 5 years from notification, so check it is still current.
evidence: Ladakh Homestay Policy 2023 PDF: eligibility, three-tier committees, incentives and owner duties.
verify_with: Assistant Director (Tourism), Leh / Kargil

question_en: How do I register my home stay in Haryana?
answer: Haryana's Home Stay Scheme (Gazette 35/2024) allows up to 5 rooms in the owner's own house, with a family member present during stays. The application fee is Rs 200 and registration is renewed every 5 years. A district committee inspects. The scheme covers areas outside municipal bodies. Rural homestays get exemption from local tax and domestic electricity and water rates.
actions: Read the Haryana Tourism Home Stay Scheme gazette.
Apply online and prepare for the inspection.
Ask the District Tourism Officer about domestic electricity and water rates.
caution: The text mentions bank loan help up to Rs 3 lakh per room with interest subsidy; confirm eligibility before counting on it.
evidence: Haryana Tourism Gazette Notification 35/2024 Home Stay scheme: up to 5 rooms, Rs 200 fee, 5-year renewal, rural tariff exemptions.
verify_with: Haryana Tourism Department / District Tourism Officer

question_en: How do I register my homestay in West Bengal?
answer: The 2022 West Bengal Homestay Tourism Policy (secondary summary) says you can apply online or at the District Magistrate's office. Fee: Rs 1,000 for Category A (Gold) and Rs 500 for B (Silver). An inspection and police verification follow, and the DM issues a certificate valid for 3 years. It also mentioned Rs 1 lakh support and domestic utility rates. A new homestay policy was planned for 2026, so check what is current.
actions: Ask the District Magistrate's tourism desk or the district tourism officer for the current policy.
Gather property papers and ID for police verification.
Check whether the 2026 policy replaced the 2022 one.
caution: The 2022 summary is a secondary source and the 2026 policy was not read.
evidence: wbxpress summary of West Bengal Homestay Tourism Policy 2022: 1-6 rooms, fees, DM certificate, 3-year validity, Rs 1 lakh support.
verify_with: District Magistrate's office / West Bengal Tourism Department

question_en: Is there a homestay policy in Uttar Pradesh and how do I register?
answer: A June 2025 news report says the UP cabinet approved a Homestay and Bed and Breakfast Policy. Units must get NOCs from the relevant local bodies. Before this, units registered only through the Ministry's NIDHI portal. Financial incentives are mentioned but details were not given.
actions: Ask the UP Tourism Department for the policy order and application route.
Get the local body NOC the policy asks for.
Keep your NIDHI registration if you already have one.
caution: Details come from a news report; the policy text was not read.
evidence: The Week (PTI) report of 3 Jun 2025 on UP Cabinet approval of Homestay and B&B Policy.
verify_with: UP Tourism Department / District Tourism Officer

question_en: How do I register my homestay in Andhra Pradesh?
answer: Andhra Pradesh has an official portal (homestays.ap.gov.in). It has five steps: create an account, apply with documents, District Tourism Officer inspection, District Level Committee review, and a digital certificate valid for 2 years. Properties can be Silver or Gold. Processing is stated as 15 to 30 days after documents are submitted. A helpdesk is listed (0866-2555525).
actions: Create an account on homestays.ap.gov.in.
Upload your documents and prepare for the DTO visit.
Call the helpdesk if you face a problem.
caution: Timelines depend on inspection. Confirm fees and documents on the portal.
evidence: AP homestay portal page: 5-step process, 2-year certificate, Silver/Gold, helpdesk numbers.
verify_with: District Tourism Officer, Andhra Pradesh / APTDC helpdesk

question_en: How do I register a Bed & Breakfast or homestay in Punjab?
answer: In Punjab, the Punjab Heritage and Tourism Promotion Board (PHTPB) registers B&B and homestay units online. Gold needs a house under 20 years old, 25 percent open space, hygienic food storage and parking. Silver is for houses that do not meet Gold but have at least one room to let. You upload photos and ID, ownership and construction papers. The certificate has lifetime validity, per the page.
actions: Open the Punjab eServices B&B page and read the Gold and Silver rules.
Take photos of kitchen, gate, parking, rooms and bathrooms.
Call PHTPB support on 0172-5078449 (10 AM to 5 PM on weekdays).
caution: Fees were not listed on the page.
evidence: Punjab eServices BnB page: categories, documents, issuing authority CEO PHTPB, lifetime validity.
verify_with: PHTPB / Punjab Department of Tourism

question_en: I am a farmer in Maharashtra. Can I run agri-tourism and homestay on my farm?
answer: Yes. The Maharashtra Tourism Policy 2024 says agri-tourism will be recognised as agri-business. A farmer may run it without a non-agricultural permit but must inform the local revenue department. The policy mentions licences for several years, domestic electricity rates for agri-tourism homestays, and temporary tents, tree houses and pods.
actions: Read the agri-tourism part of the Maharashtra Tourism Policy 2024.
Inform your tehsil or revenue office in writing that you plan agri-tourism.
Ask the Tourism Directorate how to get the agri-tourism licence.
caution: Policy text mentions both a 10-year licence and renewal every 5 years in different parts. Ask the Directorate which applies. Incentive amounts in the policy are for larger projects; small farms should ask about their category.
evidence: Maharashtra Tourism Policy 2024 PDF: agri-tourism as agri-business, no NA permit (inform revenue), domestic electricity rate, tents and tree houses.
verify_with: Maharashtra Tourism Directorate / MTDC / Tehsildar

question_en: Is there a homestay scheme in Bihar and who can apply?
answer: A 2026 news report describes the Chief Minister Homestay Promotion Scheme in Bihar. It says support up to Rs 11 lakh, up to 8 rooms, and extra for women, SHGs and youth. Government employees cannot apply. You need Aadhaar, PAN, bank and land documents, and must run the homestay for 5 years. Apply online with your mobile number.
actions: Look for the scheme on the Bihar Tourism Department portal.
Prepare Aadhaar, PAN, bank passbook and land papers.
Check if the 5-year operation rule suits your plan.
caution: This is from a news report only. Rules and amounts need confirmation.
evidence: Patna Press report on Bihar Homestay Promotion Scheme 2026.
verify_with: Bihar Tourism Department / District Tourism Officer

question_en: Can my village apply for money under Swadesh Darshan 2.0?
answer: Not directly. Under Swadesh Darshan 2.0 challenge-based destination development, a Destination Management Organisation (a local body or group set up for the destination) submits a proposal through the state government. Each state can send up to 5. The money pays mostly for soft items like training, marketing and institution building, with limited hard infrastructure. One theme is the Vibrant Village Program, with Rs 5 crore per destination for 10 destinations.
actions: Ask your District Tourism Officer whether your area is in a state proposal.
Form or join a local tourism committee with panchayat support.
Prepare a simple village tourism plan to give the state.
caution: Selection is competitive. Do not pay anyone to get a village selected.
evidence: Guidelines for Challenge Based Destination Development under SD 2.0: DMO proposals via state, 5 per state, Rs 900 crore, Vibrant Village theme Rs 5 crore each for 10 destinations.
verify_with: State Tourism Department / Ministry of Tourism

question_en: How can my village become a Best Tourism Village?
answer: The Ministry of Tourism runs a national Best Tourism Villages competition. In 2024, 36 villages won across 8 categories, including Agri Tourism, Community Based Tourism, Craft, Heritage, Responsible Tourism and Vibrant Village. There were 991 applications from 30 states and UTs. Winning gives recognition; the page read did not describe cash.
actions: Watch the Ministry of Tourism rural tourism portal for the next call.
Choose the category your village is strongest in.
Gather photos, stories and proof of community participation.
caution: A UN Tourism list exists separately; this entry covers only the Ministry's competition. Dates and criteria change each year.
evidence: Ministry of Tourism release on Best Tourism Villages Competition 2024: 36 winners, 8 categories, 991 applications.
verify_with: State Tourism Department / Ministry of Tourism (rural tourism portal)

question_en: I live in a border village. Does the Vibrant Villages Programme help with tourism?
answer: The Vibrant Villages Programme is run by the Ministry of Home Affairs. VVP-I covers 662 northern border villages and VVP-II covers 1,954 villages on all land borders. Under VVP-I, 327 tourism projects worth Rs 145 crore were approved, such as viewpoints, trek routes, eco-resorts and tourist centres. The document read does not mention homestay money.
actions: Ask your District Magistrate's office whether your village is in VVP-I or VVP-II.
Tell the tourism office about your homestay or guide plans.
Look for local project proposals through your panchayat.
caution: Border areas may need special permits for visitors. Ask local authorities before inviting guests.
evidence: PIB document Sep 2026: VVP-I 662 villages, VVP-II 1,954, 327 tourism projects, Rs 145 crore; SD 2.0 has a Vibrant Village theme (S56).
verify_with: District Magistrate / District Tourism Officer

question_en: I live in a tribal village. Is there a special homestay scheme for us?
answer: Yes, there is a central plan. Under the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan, the Ministry of Tourism says 1,000 tribal homestays are to be developed. Support mentioned: up to Rs 5 lakh for two new rooms per household, Rs 3 lakh to renovate, and up to Rs 5 lakh for community needs, with training. Your state or district decides the list of villages.
actions: Ask the District Tourism Officer or Tribal Welfare Office if your village is chosen.
Ask about training for homestay owners.
Plan your rooms to meet the scheme's standards.
caution: Amounts are scheme maximums, not guaranteed. Another Ministry answer says up to Rs 5 crore for a state or UT for 5 to 10 homestays per village in a cluster.
evidence: Ministry of Tourism Feb 2026 release and 21 Jul 2025 PIB: 1,000 tribal homestays under PM-JUGA with stated amounts.
verify_with: District Tourism Officer / Tribal Affairs Department

question_en: What is the National Strategy for Sustainable Tourism and STCI? Does it matter to a small host?
answer: It is a 2022 Ministry of Tourism strategy with seven pillars, including environment, culture, fair local benefit and a certification idea called Sustainable Tourism Criteria of India (STCI). It asks destinations to manage visitors, support local business and respect culture. For a small host it is a guide, not a licence you must hold.
actions: Use its ideas: save water and energy, buy local, and respect culture.
Ask your tourism office whether STCI certification is open in your state.
Share your sustainability steps with guests.
caution: I could not confirm if STCI certification is open to homestays today.
evidence: National Strategy for Sustainable Tourism 2022 PDF: pillars and STCI.
verify_with: Ministry of Tourism / State Tourism Department

question_en: Can I run a nature trek or camping inside forest land near my village?
answer: Inside protected forest or wildlife areas, rules are strict. The National Strategy for Ecotourism says only minimal facilities such as toilets, shelters, seasonal tents and trails are allowed, no new residential buildings, and local panchayats and forest dwellers must be consulted. It also expects fair benefit sharing with communities. Permission comes from the Forest Department.
actions: Speak to the local Forest Range Officer before you plan any activity.
Ask if a community ecotourism committee exists in your area.
Plan to use local guides and share income fairly.
caution: I could not read the MoEFCC guideline; this is from the Ministry of Tourism strategy. Never enter or operate in a protected area without written permission.
evidence: National Strategy for Ecotourism 2022 PDF: community role, benefit sharing, limits in protected areas.
verify_with: Divisional Forest Officer / Wildlife Warden

question_en: Is there any scheme for a craft village or heritage village?
answer: I could not verify a single national scheme for craft or heritage villages in this check. What I can confirm is that the Best Tourism Villages competition has Craft and Heritage categories, and Swadesh Darshan 2.0 has a culture and heritage theme for destinations. Handicraft schemes sit with other ministries.
actions: Ask your District Industries Centre about handicraft support.
Ask the tourism office about the Craft and Heritage village categories.
Document your craft traditions with the community's permission.
caution: Do not display or sell sacred or restricted cultural items without the community's consent.
evidence: Best Tourism Villages 2024 categories (S57) and SD 2.0 themes (S56). No dedicated craft village scheme was read.
verify_with: District Industries Centre / District Tourism Officer

question_en: Where can I get training in hospitality for my homestay?
answer: The Ministry of Tourism's Capacity Building for Service Providers scheme offers education, training and certification to tourism service providers and homestay owners. States also run training. Ask your tourism office for the next batch.
actions: Ask your District Tourism Officer about CBSP training near you.
Ask whether training is free or fee-based.
Join the local homestay association if there is one.
caution: Availability varies by state and year.
evidence: PIB 21 Jul 2025: CBSP scheme for training and certification of homestay owners.
verify_with: District Tourism Officer

question_en: Do I need a licence to work as a local guide for tourists?
answer: It depends on the place and the site. The Ministry of Tourism has a Regional Level Guide licence and the Incredible India Tourist Facilitator certification. Some sites, parks and states also have their own guide licence or approval. Ask the tourism office and the site authority where you plan to guide.
actions: Ask the District Tourism Officer if your state needs a guide licence.
Ask the site authority (forest, monument, trek) about its guide approval.
Think about the IITF certification for wider recognition.
caution: I did not read the Regional Level Guide rules themselves. Do not guide inside protected areas without approval.
evidence: IITFC guideline mentions Regional Level Guide licence holders (S59); no state guide licence rules were read.
verify_with: Regional Office of Ministry of Tourism / State Tourism Department

question_en: How can I become a certified Incredible India Tourist Facilitator?
answer: The IITF programme (Jan 2021 guideline) lets you register online on the IITF portal with Aadhaar or Voter ID. You must be at least 18. If you are under 40 you need class 12; if 40 or above, class 10. The guideline lists Rs 2,000 registration and Rs 500 exam fees, waived for SC/ST candidates and residents of Ladakh, J&K and aspirational districts. Certificates last 5 years.
actions: Open the IITF portal and check the current fees and dates.
Keep ID and education certificates ready.
Choose the Basic (IITF) or specialised heritage or adventure (IITG) path.
caution: Fees and rules are from a 2021 guideline and may have changed.
evidence: IITFC modified guidelines Jan 2021: eligibility, fees, levels and validity.
verify_with: IITF portal / Ministry of Tourism

question_en: I want to offer treks, rafting or camping. What safety rules apply?
answer: In July 2025 the Ministry of Tourism, with the Adventure Tour Operators Association of India, issued Model Safety Guidelines covering 29 adventure activities (15 land, 7 air, 7 water). They were sent to all states and UTs to adopt, and states were asked to enforce licensing. Your actual licence and rules depend on your state and the land or water authority.
actions: Ask your state tourism department which adventure activities need a licence.
Use trained staff, safety gear and a written emergency plan.
Check with the Forest Department for treks in forests.
caution: Do not run risky activities without licence and trained instructors. Lives are at risk.
evidence: Ministry of Tourism PIB document (July 2025): model safety guidelines, 29 activities, circulated to states.
verify_with: State Tourism Department / Adventure licensing authority

question_en: Do I need registration if I sell tour packages from my village?
answer: Rules differ by state. The Ministry of Tourism has its own recognition for tour operators and travel agents, but this is not a licence to sell packages in your state. Some states have a tourist trade registration law. If you sell packages beyond your own homestay, ask your state tourism department what registration is needed.
actions: Ask your state Tourism Department about the tourist trade or tour operator registration.
Start by selling experiences through a registered tour operator or platform.
Keep GST, PAN and business registration ready if your state needs them.
caution: I could not open the guideline details. Do not claim 'approved by the Ministry' unless you hold the approval.
evidence: No source read for tour operator registration details; method and referral only.
verify_with: State Tourism Department / Regional Office, Ministry of Tourism

question_en: I want to build guest rooms on my farm land. Do I need to change the land use?
answer: The rule is state-wise. Maharashtra's 2024 tourism policy says farmers running agri-tourism do not need a non-agricultural permit but must inform the local revenue department. Other states may need conversion or a permit from the revenue department. Ask before you build.
actions: Ask your Tehsildar or revenue office whether guest rooms on farm land need permission.
Ask the tourism office whether agri-tourism has any special relief in your state.
Get permission in writing before construction.
caution: Building on farm land without the needed permission can lead to demolition or fines. Only Maharashtra's rule was verified here.
evidence: Maharashtra Tourism Policy 2024: farmers may run agri-tourism without NA permit but must inform revenue department (S74). Other states not checked.
verify_with: Tehsildar / Revenue Department / District Tourism Officer

question_en: Will I be charged commercial electricity rates for my homestay?
answer: It depends on your state and electricity board. The Ministry's strategy suggests states give homestays domestic rates. Gujarat's policy gives residential rates; Haryana gives rural homestays domestic rates; Maharashtra gives domestic rates to agri-tourism homestays; West Bengal's 2022 policy mentions domestic utility rates. Himachal Pradesh rules (summary) charge commercial rates for homestays in urban and planning areas, and Silver category keeps domestic rates.
actions: Ask your electricity board which tariff applies to homestays.
Show your tourism registration certificate when you apply for the domestic rate.
Ask the tourism office for a letter if the policy promises domestic rates.
caution: Rates are set by each state electricity regulator. Do not change your meter category yourself.
evidence: Strategy suggestion (S54); Gujarat residential rates (S68); Haryana rural domestic rates (S70); Maharashtra agri-tourism domestic electricity (S74); WB 2022 summary (S71); HP summary (S64).
verify_with: State electricity distribution company (DISCOM) / Tourism Department

question_en: Will my house be taxed as commercial property if I take guests?
answer: It varies. Gujarat's homestay policy gives residential rates for municipal property and water tax. West Bengal's 2022 policy (summary) mentions residential property tax rates. The Centre's roadmap suggests states treat homestays as residential for water, power and property tax. Your local body decides the rate.
actions: Ask your Gram Panchayat or municipality which tax category applies.
Show your homestay registration when asking for the residential rate.
Pay all dues regularly because some schemes ask for it.
caution: Do not stop paying tax on your own. Get the decision in writing.
evidence: Gujarat policy (S68); WB 2022 summary (S71); Ministry Dec 2025 release suggestions (S50).
verify_with: Gram Panchayat / Municipal body

question_en: Do I need a trade licence or GST to run a homestay?
answer: Goa's page lists trade licences and local authority NOCs among documents, and Goa's newer process mentions GST registration only if applicable. Other states may or may not need them. GST depends on income and law, so ask a tax professional.
actions: Ask your tourism office which licences your state needs for homestay.
Ask the panchayat or municipality about a local trade licence.
Ask a tax professional or the GST office about GST.
caution: This is not tax advice. Rules changed in 2025; confirm with the GST helpdesk or a chartered accountant.
evidence: Goa Tourism page lists trade licences and NOCs (S66); Ministry Dec 2025 release says Goa asks GST registration if applicable (S50).
verify_with: District Tourism Officer / local body / GST officer

question_en: Do I need police verification for my homestay?
answer: Several policies ask for it. The older Ministry scheme text asks for a police clearance about the owner. Gujarat's policy includes police verification, and West Bengal's 2022 policy (summary) has police verification after the inspection. Ask your tourism office what your state needs.
actions: Ask the tourism office if police verification is part of your registration.
Apply at your nearest police station with ID and address proof.
Keep the certificate in your records.
caution: Rules on guest records for foreign visitors are covered in the legal domain; ask there.
evidence: Police clearance listed in scheme text (S53); Gujarat verification steps (S68); WB summary (S71).
verify_with: District Tourism Officer / local police station

question_en: Do I have to display my registration certificate or a signboard?
answer: Many states ask you to show your certificate. Kerala requires the classification certificate to be shown to guests. Gujarat asks owners to display certificates and room charges. Ladakh asks for a Proof of Listing certificate. Ask your tourism office about signboard rules.
actions: Display the certificate in your reception or entrance.
Put your room rates where guests can see them.
Replace the certificate when you renew.
caution: Rules differ by state; do not copy another state's signboard format.
evidence: Kerala guidelines (S63), Gujarat policy (S68), Ladakh policy (S69).
verify_with: District Tourism Officer

question_en: Should I show my registration number on my website or booking listing?
answer: It is a good habit and some platforms or states may ask for it. I could not verify a national rule on this. Show your registration or certificate number only if it is real and current. Do not claim Ministry approval or a Gold or Silver category you do not hold.
actions: Add your valid registration number to your listings where there is a space.
Update it after every renewal.
Ask your state whether it requires the number in advertisements.
caution: Using a fake or expired number may lead to listing removal or legal trouble.
evidence: No source read for display of registration number in ads. Method only.
verify_with: State Tourism Department / platform support

question_en: What documents will booking websites ask for to list my homestay?
answer: Each platform sets its own rules. Many ask for ID, proof of ownership or right to host, and your state registration if the state requires it. For example, one Airbnb page says Karnataka homestays must be registered with the Tourism Department. A Ministry of Tourism statement says private booking sites handle bookings, and NIDHI is not a booking site.
actions: Keep ID, ownership papers and your tourism registration ready.
Read the platform's page for your state.
Use accurate photos and describe your house honestly.
caution: Do not list rooms that are not registered if your state requires registration.
evidence: NIDHI is not a booking platform (S52); private OTAs provide booking facility (S51). Documents asked by platforms are general practice.
verify_with: Platform support / District Tourism Officer

question_en: What safety items do inspectors check in a homestay?
answer: The older Ministry scheme text lists mandatory items such as fire safety equipment, clean kitchen, 24-hour water, guest registration records and clean rooms. Himachal's 2025 rules (summary) add CCTV in common areas and fire equipment. Ask your inspector for the list for your state.
actions: Place a fire extinguisher in a clear spot and learn to use it.
Keep a guest register and first aid kit.
Test your wiring and gas connection before the inspection.
caution: Safety needs are legal and for life safety. Fire and electrical rules come from local authorities.
evidence: Ministry scheme text: fire safety, guest records, hygienic kitchen (S53). HP summary: CCTV, fire equipment (S64).
verify_with: Fire Department / District Tourism Officer

question_en: What if my homestay application is rejected or I get a lower category?
answer: Under the older Ministry scheme, the committee may suggest a lower category (no fee refund). You can fix deficiencies within 3 months and can appeal within 30 days to the committee chairman. Kerala allows appeal to the Director within 30 days. Gujarat allows appeal to the Secretary (Tourism) within 60 days. Check your state's process.
actions: Ask the inspector for the list of deficiencies in writing.
Fix them and reapply within the allowed time.
File an appeal on time if you believe the decision is unfair.
caution: Timelines differ by state. Keep copies of every document.
evidence: Scheme text (S53): 3 months to fix, appeal in 30 days; Kerala (S63) 30 days; Gujarat (S68) 60 days.
verify_with: State Tourism Department

question_en: How long is my homestay registration valid and when must I renew?
answer: It differs. The Ministry scheme text says 2 years. Kerala is 3 years, Gujarat 2 years, Andhra Pradesh 2 years, Haryana renewal every 5 years, and West Bengal's 2022 summary says 3 years. Punjab's page says lifetime validity. Reapply 3 months before expiry where the rules say so.
actions: Note your expiry date and set a reminder.
Start renewal 3 months ahead if your state asks for it.
Inform the department of changes in rooms or facilities.
caution: Validity can change when a policy is revised.
evidence: Validity from each source page: S53 2 yrs, S63 3 yrs, S68 2 yrs, S77 2 yrs, S70 5-yr renewal, S71 3 yrs, S78 lifetime.
verify_with: State Tourism Department

question_en: Can I host foreign guests in my homestay and what do I need to do?
answer: Hosting foreign guests has separate legal steps for recording and reporting. Those rules are in the legal part of this knowledge bank. Please use that guidance and check with your local police and the tourism office. This entry does not cover them.
actions: Ask the Mentor for the legal guidance on foreign guests.
Check with local police about guest reporting.
Do not host foreign guests until you know the rules.
caution: Wrong reporting can lead to penalties. Do not guess.
evidence: Refers to the legal domain; no facts stated.
verify_with: Local police / FRRO / District Tourism Officer

question_en: My state is not listed. How do I find out its homestay rules?
answer: Search for your state tourism department homestay page, or ask the District Tourism Officer. Some states have recent policies or portals (for example Odisha's Go Homestay portal or Telangana's plan), but I could not verify them here. If your state has none, the national scheme and NIDHI are your base.
actions: Ask the District Tourism Officer for any homestay order or scheme.
Check your state tourism website for homestay or bed and breakfast.
Ask the Gram Panchayat about local rules.
caution: Do not rely on websites of agents; use government pages and ask for the order number.
evidence: NIDHI as national registration database (S52). State policy names Odisha/Telangana seen only in search or news snippets and not verified.
verify_with: District Tourism Officer

question_en: Can a group of families in my village run homestays together?
answer: Yes, several policies support groups. The 2022 rural homestay strategy suggests village clusters around crafts, agri-tourism or tribal culture, with training. A May 2026 report says Uttarakhand allows groups of 8 to 10 homestays to register as Community Based Tourism Units. Ask your state about group registration.
actions: Hold a village meeting and agree who benefits and how income is shared.
Ask the tourism office about group or cluster registration.
Write rules for guest rotation so every family gets a fair share.
caution: Agree on benefit sharing in writing and protect your cultural practices.
evidence: Rural homestay strategy 2022 (S54); Uttarakhand report (S75).
verify_with: District Tourism Officer / Gram Panchayat

question_en: How do I ask for domestic rates for water and power for my homestay?
answer: Ask the tourism office for a certificate showing you are a registered homestay. Then apply to your electricity and water authority and quote your state's homestay policy. The Ministry's strategy and December 2025 roadmap both suggest residential rates for homestays, but states decide.
actions: Get a copy of your registration certificate.
Write an application to the electricity and water offices.
Keep a copy and ask for a receipt.
caution: Do not mix your home and guest meters without permission.
evidence: Strategy 2022 (S54) and Dec 2025 roadmap (S50) suggest residential rates; the process is general practice.
verify_with: DISCOM / Water authority / Tourism office
